clips.text_zh: 白銀而家抵到笑咗。個圖係好核突，但呢個就係而家個market入面最好嘅機會。唔係個d膽細鬼做到嘅。買啦，就係依家。
clips.text_en_b1: Silver is laughably cheap right now. I don't care if the chart looks bad. This is the opportunity in the market right now, but it is not for the faint of heart. Buy now. Silver has been beaten down for months and many anons think a reversal is coming soon.
clips.text_en_b2: Silver is selling at laughably cheap levels right now, and although the chart looks rough, this genuinely stands out as the most compelling opportunity in the current market. The catch is that it is not for the faint of heart, since prices have been hammered down for months. Many anons think a reversal is coming soon. Buy now.
clips.text_en_c1: Silver has become what can only be described as laughably undervalued at present levels. While the price action remains undeniably ugly, contrarians contend that this asymmetry represents the single most compelling opportunity currently available in the broader commodities space. The setup demands conviction, since meaningful gains will likely require capital that the faint of heart are unwilling to commit. After months of relentless capitulation, several anons are now positioning for an imminent reversal, arguing that the metal has been sufficiently washed out to justify aggressive accumulation on this dip.
clips.text_en_c2: Silver is presently trading at prices that border on the absurd, a once-in-a-cycle dislocation any serious investor ought to recognise for what it is. The chart, admittedly, is unlovely—months of grinding deterioration have left the metal scarred, and the prevailing sentiment among retail commentators is one of weary capitulation. That, precisely, is why the asymmetry favours the bold. Capitulation has historically marked exhaustion rather than the beginning of further decline; capital flows reverse when consensus is most uniformly bearish. Spot has been routed for the better part of a year, and a non-trivial contingent of seasoned anons now anticipate a sharp reversal within the coming weeks. This is not a trade for the squeamish. It demands conviction, and conviction, as ever, is in short supply.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread declaring silver the trade of the moment

clips.text_zh: Elon又出嚟整嘢。今次係Tesla Roadster，仲話識飛。個livestream key了個YT jank。另一邊又話starlink出咗問題throttle緊個d客——唔好笑喎，真係會輸。
clips.text_en_b1: Tesla is revealing the new Roadster tonight. Elon says it can fly. The official livestream broke, so anons are using a janky YouTube link. Hours later Musk unveiled the car on stream, calling it something between a Roadster and a spaceship. The stock and tech crowd are watching closely.
clips.text_en_b2: Tesla is unveiling the new Roadster tonight, and Elon claims it can actually fly. The official livestream crashed early on, so anons ended up relying on a janky YouTube mirror to follow along. Hours later, Musk finally rolled out the car live, describing it as something between a Roadster and a spaceship. Both the stock crowd and the tech crowd are keeping a close eye on the fallout.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk has elected to unveil the next-generation Tesla Roadster tonight, with the eccentric CEO reportedly claiming the vehicle can fly. The official livestream promptly crashed, forcing anons to cobble together a janky YouTube mirror in real time. Following several hours of technical chaos, Musk eventually presented the car on stream, branding it a hybrid somewhere between a conventional Roadster and something resembling a spaceship. Both the equity crowd and the broader technology ecosystem are watching the spectacle unfold closely.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk is preparing to unveil the next-generation Tesla Roadster this evening, a vehicle he insists he has repeatedly described as capable of flight—or, at minimum, something perilously close to it. The official livestream, in a flourish emblematic of the company's recent operational record, has already suffered a catastrophic failure, leaving anons scrambling for an unofficial YouTube mirror whose bitrate wobbles like a nervous trader's hand. Hours later, Musk eventually took to the stream and presented the car, characterising it as a hybrid somewhere between a roadster and a small spacecraft, an answer that satisfied precisely no one who wanted specifications. The crossover audience of equity watchers and technology obsessives is following closely, trying to determine what Musk has inadvertently underwritten.

clips.text_zh: China而家整到RAM出嚟？冇TSMC冇ASML冇AMAT？？西方成條chip supply chain就直接瓜？個post講到好似已經game over。睇下west啲chip equipment股連鎖反應。
clips.text_en_b1: Chinese RAM. China can now produce RAM without TSMC, ASML, or AMAT. The entire western chip production chain goes to shit. China does everything and wins. Is it truly over for the old equipment makers, or does demand still hold up for legacy nodes used in factories and infrastructure work?
clips.text_en_b2: Chinese RAM is now in production without TSMC, ASML, or AMAT, and the entire western chip supply chain is feeling the heat. China allegedly does everything and wins, which has sparked panic across the sector. The real question is whether it is truly game over for legacy equipment makers, or whether demand for older nodes used in factories and infrastructure will still hold the line.
clips.text_en_c1: Chinese RAM production has reportedly achieved a milestone that fundamentally challenges the existing western semiconductor ecosystem. According to circulating analyses, domestic manufacturers can now produce memory chips without TSMC's fabrication expertise, ASML's lithography systems, or Applied Materials' deposition technology, effectively obsoleting the legacy western chip supply chain. The discourse has shifted toward assessing whether established equipment manufacturers face structural obsolescence or whether legacy node demand from industrial and infrastructure applications remains sufficiently robust to weather the disruption.
clips.text_en_c2: The suggestion that mainland China can now produce competitive memory entirely without TSMC, ASML, or Applied Materials is, on its face, an extraordinary claim—one that, if true, would redraw the global semiconductor map overnight. The absence of those three names in any credible advanced-fabrication supply chain has long been treated as a near-insurmountable barrier, the absence of which would render much of the western equipment complex suddenly peripheral. Yet the original poster, in characteristic fashion, has framed the development as though the contest were already concluded, the victor crowned and the incumbents relegated to the dustbin of industrial history. The more judicious inquiry is whether legacy-node demand—the unglamorous workhorses of factory automation and infrastructure deployment—will hold up, or whether the contagion propagates through the entire equipment complex.

clips.text_zh: AI邊個最穩？咪就係hyperscaler囉。Google Amazon Meta Microsoft，cashflow掂，debt又頂得住。Neocloud同lab隨時歸零，得呢d big tech先唔會瓜。
clips.text_en_b1: If you want to bet on AI in the safer way, hyperscalers are the pick. Neoclouds can go to zero, frontier labs can go to zero, and chip makers can see margins collapse. But Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft fund their AI buildout mostly from cash flow. Long-term holders will be fine even if the AI trade busts.
clips.text_en_b2: The safest way to bet on AI is to go with the hyperscalers rather than the flashier picks. Neoclouds and frontier labs can easily go to zero, while chip makers may see their margins collapse overnight. By contrast, Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are funding their AI buildout largely out of operating cash flow, so long-term holders should be fine even if the AI trade eventually busts.
clips.text_en_c1: For investors seeking exposure to artificial intelligence without assuming existential vendor risk, the hyperscalers remain the prudent allocation. Frontier laboratories face outright liquidation scenarios, neoclouds can vaporize within quarters, and chip designers confront cyclical margin compression. Google, Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft, by contrast, fund their respective AI buildouts substantially through free cash flow rather than speculative debt issuance. Long-term holders should therefore remain well-positioned even in the event that the prevailing AI trade ultimately unwinds.
clips.text_en_c2: For investors seeking exposure to artificial intelligence without the attendant existential dread, the hyperscalers constitute the rational harbour in the storm. Neoclouds, those capital-hungry upstarts that have ridden the AI enthusiasm onto premium names, may evaporate to nothing; frontier laboratories, for all the considerable talent they harbour, may likewise vanish overnight; and even the chip designers, whose margins once seemed inviolable, may yet discover margin compression at scale. By contrast, Google, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft fund their vast AI capex overwhelmingly from operating cash flow, balance sheets robust enough to absorb a downturn, and businesses diversified enough that even a wholesale AI bust would leave them recognisably intact. Patient capital will be fine in modest fashion. The trade, in short, is boring—and boredom is the unsung virtue of long-horizon conviction.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about AI-safe plays being hyperscalers

clips.text_zh: ok呢條幾重要。Goodfire audit咗Qwen3-32B，九成neuron得一條主job，約7%有兩條相關job，淨低2-4%未明。即係LLM唔係咁神秘，AI末日可以cancel。
clips.text_en_b1: The AI apocalypse is cancelled. Neural network interpretability is not as hard as we thought. We might actually supervise even the biggest LLMs. In early audits of Qwen3-32B, about 90% of neuron poles have one main job, around 7% have two related jobs, and only 2 to 4 percent are not yet understood. This is a big deal for safety.
clips.text_en_b2: The AI apocalypse is officially cancelled, because neural network interpretability is turning out to be far more tractable than people assumed. Early audits of Qwen3-32B by Goodfire found that roughly 90% of neuron poles handle a single main task, around 7% manage two related ones, and only 2 to 4% remain unexplained. This effectively means we may be able to supervise even the largest LLMs. It is a big deal for safety.
clips.text_en_c1: The prospect of superintelligent AI escaping meaningful supervision may be considerably more tractable than previously assumed. Goodfire's preliminary interpretability audits of Qwen3-32B reveal that approximately ninety percent of neuron poles perform a single primary function, while roughly seven percent exhibit dual related responsibilities. A residual two to four percent remain uncharacterized. Such empirical findings suggest that large language models are far less inscrutable than conventional wisdom holds, with profound implications for alignment research and regulatory frameworks.
clips.text_en_c2: The much-anticipated AI apocalypse may, on closer examination, be cancelled—or at least postponed pending further empirical review. Interpretability, that most elusive of grails within contemporary neural network research, appears to be rather less intractable than the prevailing doomer consensus would suggest, provided one is willing to conduct the requisite audits rather than merely speculate from first principles. Goodfire's preliminary investigations into Qwen3-32B yield results that, while preliminary, are nonetheless striking: approximately ninety per cent of neuronal poles appear to perform one principal task, around seven per cent have two related tasks, and one.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on neural net interpretability progress

clips.text_zh: Elon個MAGA百萬美金抽獎全部內定。2024個PAC呃人話有random贏，結果輸咗個class action lawsuit。原來所謂嘅萬分之一機會都係揀出嚟嘅。
clips.text_en_b1: Elon's MAGA $1M Winners were predetermined. His political action committee told voters they had a random chance to win a million dollars in 2024, but the winners were pre-selected. A class action lawsuit was settled on Thursday over fraud allegations. Real odds were basically zero for any random voter.
clips.text_en_b2: Elon's MAGA million-dollar winners were pre-selected rather than randomly drawn, which has now blown up in court. Back in 2024, his political action committee told voters they had a genuine shot at winning a million dollars, but the entire scheme was rigged from the start. A class action lawsuit was settled on Thursday over fraud allegations, and the real odds for any ordinary voter were essentially zero.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk's purportedly random million-dollar MAGA giveaway has been exposed as a carefully orchestrated exercise in voter persuasion rather than genuine chance. His political action committee marketed the 2024 sweepstakes as offering ordinary citizens a one-in-millions probability of winning, yet internal documentation subsequently revealed that recipients were pre-selected to maximize demographic impact. A federal class action alleging deceptive solicitation was settled on Thursday, effectively confirming that the headline odds were functionally zero for any unselected participant.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk's ostensibly populist million-dollar giveaway, a spectacle that dominated much of the 2024 electoral news cycle and burnished his reputation as a man of the people, was in fact a carefully stage-managed exercise in manufactured enthusiasm. His political action committee, in language calculated to convey serendipity, assured prospective voters that they had been selected at random to receive a life-changing sum, the implication being that civic engagement might yet prove unexpectedly lucrative. The reality, as class action litigants have alleged and the settlement will address, was rather more prosaic, the recipients having been pre-selected, the ostensible lottery a veneer over a preordained outcome.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on Musk PAC lawsuit settlement

clips.text_zh: 減咗100磅都仲未搵到GF。以前275磅，去咗gym兩年半，落到179，睇落ok。但返工啲女人對我好咗，又唔知係咪純粹新工。睇完好毒。
clips.text_en_b1: I lost 100 lbs and still have no gf. I never had one and used to be 275 lbs. My sister's husband took me to the gym and told me I'd find a gf fast if I lost weight. 2.5 years later I'm 179 lbs and look pretty fit, but still no gf.
clips.text_en_b2: I dropped a full hundred pounds and I still do not have a girlfriend, which honestly stings more than I expected. I never had one growing up, and I used to weigh 275 pounds. My sister's husband eventually dragged me to the gym and swore I would find someone quickly once I lost weight. Two and a half years later, I am 179 pounds and look pretty fit. Women at work are nicer to me, but it might just be the new job.
clips.text_en_c1: Following a dramatic hundred-pound weight reduction spanning two and a half years, the poster laments a conspicuous absence of romantic prospects despite having shed what amounted to nearly a third of his former body weight. Initially weighing 275 pounds, he was taken to the gym by his sister's husband, who confidently assured him that romantic success would inevitably follow such a transformation. Now a lean 179 pounds, he observes that female colleagues treat him markedly better, though he remains uncertain whether this reflects genuine attraction or merely the novelty of his recent professional transition.
clips.text_en_c2: Having shed a not-inconsiderable hundred pounds over the course of two and a half years, one might reasonably have expected commensurate returns in the romantic arena, yet the protagonist of this particular transformation finds himself, as ever, unattached. He began his odyssey at a frankly substantial two hundred and seventy-five pounds, a body that had long since rendered him, in his own estimation at least, effectively invisible to the fairer sex; his sister's husband, in a well-intentioned if ultimately misplaced act of familial intervention, had undertaken to remedy this state of affairs by escorting him to a local gym and assuring him that corporeal improvement would, in due course, deliver the companion he so evidently craved.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about transformation with no romantic payoff

clips.text_en_b2: Weekly Shonen Jump issue #47 for 2026 features Nue on the cover alongside LCP, the new anime announcement, Hertz, One Piece, Ichi, Kiyoshi, a Sakamoto Akane color page, Roku, Ura, Graykeith, and The Young Witch and Teacher one-shot. Looking ahead to issue #48, the lineup includes Kagurabachi, Witch Watch, Shinobi, Roboco, Under Doctor, Animal Signal, Hal, and 2B Cannon Master. Plenty to look forward to.
clips.text_en_c1: The forthcoming Weekly Shonen Jump lineup has generated considerable anticipation among enthusiasts, particularly given the inclusion of a highly anticipated second one-shot installment. The forthcoming issue features a new Cinderella witch one-shot alongside established serialization entries including One Piece, the latest Demon Slayer arc, and Sakamoto. Returning favorites such as Kagurabachi, Witch Watch, and Shinobi continue their respective runs, while the new Inugami and Suzune one-shot represents the editorial highlight that the forthcoming issue collects.
clips.text_en_c2: The forthcoming edition of Weekly Shonen Jump promises a characteristically crowded slate of features, its pages seemingly designed to test the limits of even the most dedicated reader's endurance. Leading the lineup is Nenú on the cover, whose prominence reflects a status fast approaching that of marquee attraction, accompanied by LCP, whose new anime announcement has been the subject of considerable speculation among the more fanatically inclined. The remainder of the issue features a roster that reads rather like a roll-call of the contemporary shonen ecosystem: Hertz, One Piece, Ichi, Kiyoshi, a colour page from Sakamoto Akane, Roku, Ura, Graykeith, a one-shot collaboration between The Young Witch and Teacher, the perennially divisive Kagurabachi, Witch Watch, Shinobi, Roboco, Under Doctor, Animal Signal, Hal, and 2B Cannon, whose inclusion as the feature leads out of the issue…
